purpose: Test hypothesis H on a frozen independent panel: does Dynamic DAG's feedback-driven local recovery produce net benefit over Single LLM under specific fault/budget conditions? NOT a search efficiency experiment.

hypothesis.H: In conditions where observable, repairable faults constitute a high proportion and the resource budget permits, Dynamic DAG can partially recover decomposition-induced quality loss through feedback-driven local recovery, and achieve higher budget-within-completion-rate than the Single LLM baseline in predefined state and budget ranges.
hypothesis.pre_registration: state strata and budget ranges defined BEFORE any execution; no post-hoc cherry-picking of favorable conditions

three_possible_outcomes.conditional_net_benefit: Dynamic DAG achieves net benefit in some predefined conditions, replicated on independent tasks → paper claims conditional net benefit
three_possible_outcomes.quality_cost_tradeoff: Dynamic DAG has higher quality but higher cost → paper claims existence of a trade-off, adoption depends on budget
three_possible_outcomes.no_net_benefit: Single LLM is not worse in any validated condition → paper contribution repositioned as recoverable execution mechanism + applicability boundary analysis

task_panel.source: TAT-QA train, hybrid_pool() held-out UIDs excluding ALL previously used panels
task_panel.exclusions: main120, frozen200, P1-B 5 tasks, FULLVAL 4 tasks, V2 campaign 8 tasks
task_panel.freeze: UIDs + content_sha256 committed before any model call
task_panel.note: 50 tasks for adequate power for McNemar on ~15pp differences; task-level paired design

strategies.attribution_note: B/C/D/E use THE SAME frozen DAG topology (4-node e1∥e2→r→v), THE SAME prompt interfaces, and THE SAME model assignment (e1/e2=large, r=medium, v=coder) for mechanism attribution. The ONLY differences between arms are the target factors (decomposition, heterogeneity, recovery scope). V2's best-found config is tested as a SEPARATE pre-registered competitive candidate (see v2_candidate below), NOT as a replacement for any attribution arm.

v2_candidate.role: pre-registered competitive candidate from V2 campaign's best search result
v2_candidate.selection_rule: from V2 campaign's 18-session results, the config with highest mean Q across states; selection uses ONLY V2's 8 campaign tasks (NOT this protocol's 50 held-out tasks); rule frozen before this protocol's execution
v2_candidate.isolation: tested as additional arms (V2_static, V2_dynamic) alongside the attribution arms; results compared separately; NEVER substituted into B/C/D/E attribution comparisons
v2_candidate.purpose: answers 'is the search-found config competitive?' NOT 'what is the mechanism attribution?'

A_single_cross_fallback.description: Single LLM with cross-model fallback on parse failure (large → medium → coder)
A_single_cross_fallback.role: competitive baseline — tests whether DAG's benefit is just 'extra model attempts'
A_single_cross_fallback.retry: max 1 fallback per task, triggered by unparseable output only
A_single_cross_fallback.fairness_note: A' has NARROWER detection (parse-only) than D (parse + expression-exec + verification consistency); this asymmetry is documented; if D > A', the surplus is attributable to broader detection + structural recovery, not just extra attempts; however, D > A' alone does not prove structural benefit over a hypothetical single-LLM-with-full-detection baseline (which is not implementable without decomposition)

B_same_model_dag.description: 4-node DAG, all nodes use same model (large)

C_static_hetero_dag.role: isolates heterogeneity effect; SAME config as D minus recovery

D_dynamic_dag.description: Same topology/model as C + feedback-driven local recovery (Z=LOCAL_REROUTE)
D_dynamic_dag.recovery: detection on parse/exec/verification failure; reroute to alternative model; descendant closure; one attempt
D_dynamic_dag.vs_C: identical to C except recovery; ΔQ_recovery = Q_D − Q_C is the clean recovery effect

E_full_replay.description: Same detection and recovery target as D but full-graph re-execution on trigger
E_full_replay.recovery: detection SAME as D; recovery target SAME as D; ONLY difference is re-execution scope (full DAG vs affected subgraph)
E_full_replay.vs_D: ΔQ_scope = Q_E − Q_D isolates the scope effect; D and E share identical detection rules, identical recovery triggers, identical alternative models

states.fault10: 10% tasks faulted, Random(20261023) on this panel's UIDs
states.fault_model: persistent capability fault on (task, node, planned_model); answer-replacement (no extra request for injection itself); bit-identical draw rule from frozen200
states.pre_registration: fault draw computed and committed BEFORE execution; same draw used across all strategies (paired)

exposure_fairness.problem: Single LLM has 1 node; DAG has 4 nodes; same fault draw does NOT guarantee equal fault impact across strategies
exposure_fairness.node_selection: fault node drawn uniform from {e1,e2,r,v}; for Single A: fault applied to the single call if the drawn node maps to it (all nodes map to the single call since Single is undecomposed — see mapping below)
exposure_fairness.single_mapping: for A/A', all node faults (e1/e2/r/v) map to the single LLM call; fault ALWAYS exposes in A; in DAG, fault exposes only if the DAG actually executes the faulted (task,node,model) triple
exposure_fairness.exposure_audit: for each faulted task, record: which node was faulted, which strategy actually executed the faulted triple, how many times; report as exposure_matrix
exposure_fairness.fairness_note: unequal exposure is INHERENT to comparing different execution structures; it is reported transparently (exposure_matrix) rather than artificially equalized; the paired comparison remains valid (same task, same fault draw) but the MECHANISM of impact differs by structure

states.seed_replication: each fault rate uses ONE seed from the frozen set (20261023/24/25); one draw per rate is acknowledged as a limitation; multiple seeds per rate deferred to follow-up if primary result is borderline

budgets.metric: Q_B(strategy) = (# tasks correct AND total_tokens ≤ B) / n_tasks
budgets.note: post-hoc from complete trajectories; NOT online hard budget cutoff
budgets.primary_comparison: ΔQ_B(s) = Q_B(D | s) − Q_B(A | s) at each (state, budget) pair

objectives.Q: final answer correctness via scoring contract v2.1 (score_v21 + GOLD_CONTRACT_V1)
objectives.C_logical: logical execution cost (see cost_accounting): total tokens from source records for all logical calls
objectives.L_service_demand: serial service-demand reconstruction (sum of individual latency_s from source records; NOT real E2E wall-clock)

state_budget_pair.selection_rule: pre-specified from domain knowledge: 30% fault is the condition where recovery is hypothesized to help most; B*=3000 is the smallest budget where dynamic DAG trajectories are expected to complete
state_budget_pair.no_post_hoc: this (state, budget) pair is the SOLE confirmatory test; all other pairs are exploratory

primary_confirmatory.secondary_confirmatory: ΔQ_B = Q_B(D|fault30,B*) − Q_B(A'|fault30,B*) tests whether D beats the competitive fallback baseline
primary_confirmatory.test_statistic: paired task-level: exact McNemar on correct-within-budget indicators
primary_confirmatory.significance_level: α = 0.05 two-sided, no correction needed for the 2 confirmatory tests (pre-specified); Holm correction applied to remaining 38 exploratory pairs

exploratory.all_other_qb_pairs: ΔQ_B at remaining 38 (state, budget) combinations; Holm-corrected; reported as exploratory
exploratory.plain_q_comparison: A vs D raw accuracy at each state; reported as secondary analysis
exploratory.subgroup_analyses: detectable vs undetectable fault tasks; recovery success rate; recovery cost overhead

statistical_tests.confidence_intervals: task-cluster bootstrap 95% CI for all differences
statistical_tests.power_note: 50 tasks with ~15 faulted tasks at 30%; exact McNemar with 15 discordant pairs (all Help, no Harm) gives p=0.000122 — sufficient for large recovery effects; moderate effects (~8/15 Help) give p~0.0078; small effects (~5/15) give p~0.0625 (underpowered); power analysis from historical Help/Harm distribution recommended before final freeze

pre_specified_subgroups.detectable_fault_tasks: tasks where the injected fault is detectable by the frozen detection rules (mechanism detectability, determined from fault type and detection rule BEFORE execution; NOT deployment observability)
pre_specified_subgroups.undetectable_fault_tasks: tasks where the fault is NOT detectable by frozen rules (recovery cannot help)
pre_specified_subgroups.recovery_success_rate: among mechanism-detectable fault tasks, % where D recovers to correct answer
pre_specified_subgroups.recovery_cost_overhead: average extra logical tokens for D vs C on faulted tasks
pre_specified_subgroups.subgroup_note: mechanism detectability (frozen rules + fault type) is distinct from deployment detectability (runtime observability); only mechanism detectability is used for pre-specified subgroup analysis; deployment detectability would require separate online decision experiments

sample_size.n_strategies: 6 attribution arms + up to 2 V2-candidate arms
sample_size.n_evaluations: 50 × 6 × 4 = 1200 attribution evaluations (+ up to 200 V2-candidate evaluations)
sample_size.estimated_calls_per_eval: A: 1, A': 1-2, B/C: 4, D: 4-7, E: 4-8 (LOGICAL calls; physical reduced by cache reuse)
sample_size.estimated_total_physical_requests: ~2000-3500 (cache reuse reduces physical; logical stays full)

power_analysis.confirmatory_test: fault30 state: ~15 faulted tasks of 50; exact McNemar on budget-within-completion indicators
power_analysis.moderate_recovery: 8 Help / 4 Harm → p=0.115 (underpowered for sole confirmatory)
power_analysis.conclusion: 50 tasks is a PILOT-scale validation; sufficient for strong recovery effects (≥10pp net recovery gain on faulted tasks); NOT adequate for moderate effects; if confirmatory test is borderline, larger panel recommended before paper claim
power_analysis.recommendation: estimate actual Help/Harm distribution from historical fault30 paired records before execution to refine power estimate

budget.physical_vs_logical_note: per_strategy_per_state_physical_max = 400 limits PHYSICAL new requests (not logical calls); 50 tasks × 4 nodes = 200 logical base calls + recovery extras; with cache reuse, physical requests should be well under 400; if physical cap truncates a strategy, it is logged as INCOMPLETE for that state
budget.no_logical_cap: no cap on logical calls (strategies must complete their full trajectory for fair evaluation)
budget.budget_reservation: D and E strategies reserved 800 physical requests minimum (to prevent earlier strategies from consuming the budget needed for recovery evaluations)

execution_order.full_matrix: ALL 6 strategies × ALL 4 states = 24 strategy-state combinations × 50 tasks = 1200 evaluations (matches sample_size)
execution_order.rationale: Clean first to populate cache; faulted states after (reusing cache for unfaulted nodes); A' participates in ALL faulted states (critical: tests whether DAG benefit is just extra model attempts); B also participates in faulted states (isolates decomposition effect under fault)
execution_order.ordering_within_phase: A → A' → B → C → D → E (cheapest first to maximize cache reuse for expensive strategies)

cost_accounting.dual_track: two separate cost metrics, never mixed

logical_cost.definition: total tokens a strategy would consume executing ALL its nodes from scratch (cold-run), including faulted attempts and recovery
logical_cost.source: sum of usage from MeteredExecutor ledger for each logical call in the strategy's trajectory, using source-recorded usage even for cache-alias calls
logical_cost.purpose: strategy quality-cost comparison, budget-within-completion-rate Q_B, Pareto analysis
logical_cost.note: this is the FAIR comparison metric: each strategy's cost reflects its full execution, independent of execution order

physical_spend.definition: actual new model requests issued during the experiment
physical_spend.purpose: experiment resource monitoring, cache savings measurement, total experiment cost
physical_spend.note: this reflects experiment efficiency, NOT strategy cost; never used for Q_B or strategy comparison

service_latency.definition: serial service-demand reconstruction (sum of individual latency_s from source records)
service_latency.purpose: supplementary resource dimension; NOT real E2E wall-clock

cost_accounting.rule: Q_B and all strategy-vs-strategy cost comparisons use LOGICAL cost; physical spend is reported separately as experiment overhead; cache savings = logical_cost − physical_spend per strategy

cache_sharing.identity: (model_binding, prompt_sha256, task_uid, node_name, scope) from smoke_runner.py:114
cache_sharing.clean_to_fault_reuse: unfaulted nodes' prompts are state-independent → cache hits allowed
cache_sharing.fault_injection: answer replaced AFTER call; injected answer NEVER cached; underlying response cached for cost reference

scoring.gold_source: v2.1 contract gold (native_answer for percent; derived for no-scale)
scoring.version_control: both Q_v1 and Q_v2_1 recorded; Q_v2_1 is canonical

must_pass_before_execution: V2 campaign completes (provides best DAG candidates for V2-candidate arms)
Scoring path audit (GOLD_CONTRACT_V1 verified in running evaluator)
Fault injection path audit (injection replaces answer, not extra call)
Cost accounting audit (logical vs physical separation in running code)
Cache-order invariance test: same strategy's logical tokens identical regardless of execution order (cache hits vs cold)
D/E detection equivalence test: identical detection rules, identical triggers, only scope differs
prerequisites.v2_candidate_freeze_rule: V2's config selection rule frozen BEFORE this protocol's 50 tasks are executed; selection uses ONLY V2's 8 campaign tasks; NEVER uses this protocol's 50 tasks for tuning or filtering

non_claims: Does NOT prove DAG is universally better than Single
Does NOT prove search efficiency (that is V2 campaign)
Does NOT test multi-turn recovery (single recovery attempt only)
Does NOT claim real E2E deployment latency
Pre-defined conditions only; no post-hoc condition selection
